Lessons.Title: Multiply Three- and Four-digit Numbers by One-digit Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit number by decomposing factors by place value, finding partial products, and using properties of operations.
In the previous lesson, you represented multiplication using base-ten diagrams and rectangular diagrams, and used place value reasoning to multiply two-digit numbers by one-digit numbers. In this lesson, you use rectangular diagrams and expressions to multiply up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers. You continue to use place value reasoning to decompose the multi-digit factor and to use partial products in your computation.
Core relationship: Multiply three/four-digit by one-digit numbers. Use place-value partitions and regroup where necessary.

Local publisher 2021 source lesson activities: Warm-up:  Estimation Exploration: Mysterious Area	 (10 minutes); Activity 1:  Larger Numbers to Multiply	 (15 minutes); Activity 2:  Jada’s Errors	 (20 minutes); Cool-down:  The Value of the Product	 (5 minutes)
Original visual/physical and peer-explanation activities still require teacher review.
